chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Aban, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a woman who died before her husband entered into her (consummated the marriage): what is her share of the dowry, and how is her inheritance? He said: 'If he had fixed a dowry for her, she is entitled to half of the dowry, and he inherits her. And if he had not fixed a dowry for her, she inherits him, and there is no dowry for her.'
ai.seo_question: What are the dowry and inheritance rules for a wife who dies before marital consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial status of a wife who dies before consummation, distinguishing between cases where a specific dowry (Mahr) was fixed versus those where it was not. In the former, she is entitled to half the specified dowry and the husband inherits from her; in the latter, she inherits from him but receives no dowry, reflecting the principle that the right to inheritance is contingent upon the establishment of the marital bond's financial obligations. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the distribution of estate and dowry in pre-consummation death scenarios.
